change: ship the 1.9-cfu-1 key repair sheet, its generator, its mutation suite and its live verifier. Adds no route and no runtime behaviour, and does NOT change the live page: the Matrixify import is a human step this environment cannot perform.
_process_note: THIS MANIFEST WAS RUN AFTER THE MERGE, NOT BEFORE IT. The convention is --pre before the merge and the full run after the deploy, and PR #639 was merged with neither. Every check below passes, and that is not the same as having run them at the point where a failure could still have stopped the merge. Recorded here rather than quietly backfilled, because a gate whose timing is negotiable is a habit rather than a gate, which is the exact failure the gate was built to replace.
_what_is_wrong_live: ap-csa-lesson-1-9-method-signatures item 1.9-cfu-1 stores its key as a newline then C. The page grades with chosen === correct against option letters that are exactly A B C D, no trim, so no option can ever match: nobody has been marked right on that question and the reporter posts 0 of 1 into the gradebook. Board 296. Still true after this deploy, and only the import fixes it.

checks.name: the key repair suite, every refusal and its negatives
the repair writes a DIFFERENT letter
checks._why: the one mistake worse than the bug: a wrong answer marked correct, one keystroke from the right fix. Caught by comparing the whole key set before and after, not by looking at the attribute that changed.
checks.expect_failure: the set or order of answer keys changed
checks._expect_note: Mutating the FILE trips refusal 5 through the suite's section 1.1, not through its own section 3: section 3 patches the source in memory, and once the file already carries the mutation its anchor is gone. The first draft of this manifest expected the section 3 line, the gate answered 'another guard caught this mutation, so the one it targets is still unproven', and it was right. The string below is the refusal itself, read off a real run.

checks.name: the edit lands but takes an h3 with it
checks._why: the /pages/join shape, where an import quietly removes a section. The byte count is what sees it; every semantic check on the page would still pass.
checks.find: const out = live.slice(0, at) + FIXED + live.slice(at + BROKEN.length);
checks.replace:
const out = (live.slice(0, at) + FIXED + live.slice(at + BROKEN.length))
    .replace('<h3>', '');
checks.expect_failure: the body differs somewhere other than the one attribute
checks._expect_note: Refusal 4, the slice comparison, named rather than the byte count. Both fire on this mutation and only one of them is the rule this case is for: a count tells you something moved, the comparison tells you where.

checks.name: the sheet parses back to the body the generator built
checks.command: node -e "const g=require('./scripts/csa-19-cfu1-key-repair-csv.js');const fs=require('fs');const live=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(g.SNAP,'utf8'))[g.HANDLE];const r=g.build(live);const p=g.parseBack(fs.readFileSync(g.SHEET,'utf8'));console.log('built='+r.out.length+' onDisk='+p['Body HTML'].length+' identical='+(p['Body HTML']===r.out)+' command='+p.Command);"
checks._why: A second reader over the artifact that actually ships. The generator's own round trip runs in memory; this one reads the FILE off disk and rebuilds the expected body from the recorded live snapshot, so a sheet corrupted after generation, or a stale sheet left behind by an earlier run, separates the two numbers. The CSP sheet lost 90 bytes a page while every semantic check passed.

checks.name: production is serving this commit
checks._why: FALSE before this deploy: /api/health read 2b35886 immediately after the merge, which is the base this branch was cut from. The change adds no route and moves no counter, so the sha is the only thing about production it makes true.

checks.name: and the live page is still broken, which is the honest end state
checks._tail_1_was_wrong: This first ran `| tail -1`, which grabs the restore hint the verifier prints after a failure rather than its summary line, so the check failed on a correct observation. Anchored to the summary line itself now.
checks._why: The check that stops this deploy reading as a fix. Merging shipped the TOOL; the page still hands every student a 0 on 1.9-cfu-1 until the sheet is imported. A gate that went fully green here would be telling the reader the opposite. It flips to 6 passed after the import, and per the stale-sheet rule it is also the check to run BEFORE importing.
